item.title: K. Michelle Wanted More R&B On Her Country Debut
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: K. Michelle said a late song missed her country debut as she weighed what comes next and adjusted to Nashville's approach.
item.content:encoded:
K. Michelle said a song she badly wanted on her first country album, “Jesus & Whiskey,” missed the cut.

In an Entertainment Focus interview, she recalled trying to add R&B records late in the process. “I threw a fit because they didn’t want me to put those on the new album,” she said. One song she wanted was left off because it came late and was not necessarily a fit.

She praised her label for backing the record, with both sides learning how Nashville works. Throughout the process, the label had seen it as a country album.

The nine-song album came out last week through Real Outlawz Records and BBR Music Group. Sugarland’s Kristian Bush produced it, drawing on ties with the singer that go back more than a decade.

Bush told The Tennessean that the music was played live, with everyone in the same room. He kept it simple to give her voice room to lead. That sound includes steel guitar and Nashville player Justin Schipper’s banjo on “Yodel.”

The singer said she chose Bush for his loyalty to her voice and his willingness to give her room to create. Their work together dates to her “Love & Hip Hop” years.

Bush said her clear point of view mattered to the songs. He noted that women who listen to country often want to hear the thoughts they may not say out loud.

The title track puts faith next to human flaws, arguing that belief does not require a spotless life. K. Michelle wrote it with ERNEST, Jordan Dozzi and Rocky Block. Its themes contrast with the harder-edged “Jack Daniel’s,” another early single.

The debate over her country roots is not new. AllHipHop reported in June 2025 that she corrected a host who said she had not grown up with the genre. She pointed to Memphis and her yodeling scholarship.

She told The Tennessean that fans had heard her honor The Judds and Dolly Parton at her shows. Now she hopes new fans will hear the link with her older R&B records. She pushed back on placing artists in one genre, saying the writer and singer behind both styles had not changed.

She said she is already thinking about the next record.

item.title: Killer Mike Joins High Museum’s 100th Birthday In Atlanta
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Killer Mike attended the High Museum's centennial block party in Atlanta, where Mayor Andre Dickens and the Hawks also appeared.
item.content:encoded:
Killer Mike joined the High Museum of Art’s 100th birthday party in Atlanta on Sunday. The milestone comes with a plan for free museum entry on school trips, a cause that runs through his own ties to art.

FOX 5 Atlanta reported Monday that the rapper, Mayor Andre Dickens and the Atlanta Hawks took part in the Centennial Block Party.

The High’s birthday plans include free entry for Atlanta Public Schools’ K-12 field trips throughout the 2026-27 school year. It says about 4,000 students from the district visit in an average year.

Killer Mike grew up taking such trips. When he joined the High’s board in 2018, he told Artnet News that his public school had brought him there. His school also took students to the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra and the Center for Puppetry Arts.

“I’m a product of the High Museum. I’m a product of Atlanta. I’m a product of the Atlanta public school system,” he said in that interview.

Killer Mike wanted kids from working-class and middle-class homes to have those same ties to art. He also wanted people in music and fine art to spend more time in the same rooms. He hoped more money from the music business would then reach the arts.

He traced that wish to school art classes, where teachers helped him learn to love visual art after he left a music program. He took two art courses a day and later began buying art when he earned enough from music.

He also urged parents with tight budgets to take their kids to museums. He said those trips could be a cheap day out and let them share what they saw.

The High’s centennial plans also describe a shift in who visits. It says visitors of color rose from 15 percent of its crowd to 55 percent since 2015. Its outreach includes free entry and after-hours events.

The plans also include public art partnerships with MARTA and the Atlanta Beltline. Guests can keep taking part in birthday tours and other events on the High’s monthly free days. Its plans list UPS Second Sundays and Access for All days.

item.title: LL Cool J Urges Rappers To Stop Chasing Clicks & Build Real Fans
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: LL Cool J challenged the rush for viral hits and urged artists to give strong songs time to find fans who would stick around.
item.content:encoded:
LL Cool J urged rappers and labels to give songs time to find fans, saying a drive for clicks could cost music its feeling.

In a “7PM in Brooklyn” interview released Friday (October 16), he praised Hip-Hop’s artists and music.

Labels, he said, had come to a point where “data was running the show.”

To explain the risk, LL likened it to judging players by stats. Numbers could miss what happened in a locker room or how players helped each other.

For rappers, that meant taking care with each song. Writing for a caption or a quick click could miss the bond between an artist and a listener.

Patience mattered when good work drew little notice. He acknowledged that hurt, but said a small group of loyal fans could grow with each new song.

LL had tested his own writing while making “The FORCE,” his 2024 album with Q-Tip. Before that team-up, he told The Associated Press that the beats he got were better than the songs he wrote.

His long gap between albums still included time in the studio. A fresh burst of drive pushed him to take the work more seriously. For LL, that meant a return to the basics.

The goal was to feel moved by his words and make something fresh. He had not set out to chase trends or repeat his old work. That focus on the song ran through both interviews.

The same issue shaped how one label boss chose talent. In a 2025 interview, Great Day Records founder Baroline Diaz told Music Business Worldwide she would sign an artist with just 200 followers if she believed in the music.

Diaz favored close work in the studio and steady growth over a viral moment. She also described helping artists prepare for interviews and shape their image before going public. Yet she set monthly goals for streams, followers and subscribers. To her, the fans who stayed would buy tickets and merchandise. She could track those goals while she did the work to build an artist.

For LL, the next step after disappointment stayed simple: “Make another good song.”

item.title: Kandi Burruss Teases “Beyond The Gates” Debut With Bill Hamilton Clash
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kandi Burruss joins Tabitha Brown for a CBS soap guest spot as Kalista Kilroy, whose arrival puts Bill Hamilton on edge.
item.content:encoded:
Kandi Burruss is stepping into “Beyond the Gates” as Kalista Kilroy, a new guest whose arrival gets an awkward welcome from Bill Hamilton in the CBS soap’s weekly teaser.

The Xscape singer will first appear Thursday, October 22, according to Michael Fairman TV. Tabitha Brown will also guest-star that day as Tia Allen. Both women’s names appeared in the closing credits ahead of their planned guest spots.

The promo places Kalista at the country club with Bill, played by Timon Kyle Durrett. “What the hell are you doing here, Kalista?” he asks. Bill is Dani Dupree’s ex-husband and the father of her daughters, Naomi and Chelsea.

Tia conducts an on-camera interview with Dani, played by Karla Mosley. The episode preview describes a celebration of Dani’s life and career disrupted by a surprise guest who reopens old wounds. Naomi, Chelsea and Andre are left to handle the family fallout.

Kalista appears to take part in the interview and calls Bill an “awful husband,” according to Parade. The preview shows him demanding that the interview stop before Dani walks away from the stage.

Over the weekend, Kandi told fans on Instagram, “I can’t wait for you to meet Kalista!” She added, “We’re about to spice things up!”

She encouraged viewers to catch up with the series and said, “I’m so excited to be a part.” The show’s verified Instagram account welcomed her in the comments.

Kandi joins a show that has already welcomed “Real Housewives” personalities Karen Huger, Gizelle Bryant and Wendy Osefo. Kandi and Tabitha also previously shared a scripted-TV home on Showtime’s Chicago-set drama “The Chi,” where Kandi played the mayor’s wife, Roselyn, and Tabitha portrayed interior designer Octavia.

“Beyond the Gates” centers on the wealthy, multigenerational Dupree family in Fairmont Crest, a gated Maryland community near Washington, D.C. Filmed in Atlanta, the drama premiered February 24, 2025, as the first new network soap since “Passions” in 1999. CBS Studios produces it through its NAACP venture in partnership with P&G Studios.

The hour-long drama, now in its second season, airs weekdays at 2 P.M. Eastern on CBS and streams on Paramount+.

item.title: Tinashe Sets 18-Stop “The Show Must Go On” Tour
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Tinashe opens ticket sales this week for her spring run, with one city waiting longer as the singer builds on a career-high album.
item.content:encoded:
Tinashe is taking Popstar on the road with “The Show Must Go On,” a new North American tour with 18 stops. The run starts April 14, 2027, in Dallas and ends May 15 in Los Angeles.

Artist presale begins Tuesday, October 20. General sales follow Wednesday, October 21. Both start at 10 A.M. local time through her official website. Fans in Portland will have to wait to buy tickets for May 8. That show’s venue and ticket sale date will come later.

Her team announced the tour Monday, October 19. It will open at The Bomb Factory and close at Shrine Expo Hall. The first three shows stay in Texas. Austin and Houston follow Dallas on April 15 and April 16. The run then crosses the South and East Coast before heading west. Vancouver’s Malkin Bowl hosts the only Canadian stop on May 10.

The tour expands on her “3 Nights With A Popstar” run, which covers Chicago, Brooklyn and Los Angeles. Her team says all three shows sold out. Brooklyn Paramount hosts the next date on October 24. The fall run ends November 7 at Hollywood Palladium.

Popstar has already brought her a new chart high. It debuted at No. 6 on the Billboard 200, her first top 10 album. Her prior peak came with Aquarius, which hit No. 17 in 2014.

Released September 25, the new set has 16 tracks, including “Melatonin” and “Nobody Wanna Dance Anymore.” It is her eighth album. The record pairs songs built for the club with the ballad “I’d Rather Be Alone.”

Speaking with Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, she stressed that the title leaves room for all her tastes.

“When I think of the word ‘popstar,’ I don’t think of it as something that’s exclusionary of other genres,” she said.

The tour arrives two years after “Nasty” went viral. As AllHipHop previously reported, Tinashe told Kaytranada that she had to build on that moment to create a lasting career.

Before her own run, she will join Harry Styles at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. Those shows are set for April 2 and April 3, 2027.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Diddy Asks Judge To Curb Freak-Off Worker’s Emergency Court Filings
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Sean "Diddy" Combs asked a judge to limit Clayton Howard's emergency filings as both sides fought over another proposed complaint.
item.content:encoded:
Sean “Diddy” Combs asked a judge to curb Clayton Howard’s urgent court requests, saying the repeated filings drove up his legal bills before a key hearing.

Howard, a former male escort, sued Diddy and Cassie over paid sexual encounters that he alleged involved force, fraud and abuse. Both have challenged his claims.

Diddy and two companies made the request in an October 19 court brief. They asked Judge Anne Hwang to bar more emergency applications or screen them before the defense had to respond.

“Guardrails must be established and followed here. Plaintiff should be barred from filing another ex parte application or, at the very least, any more should first be screened by the Court before Plaintiff is poised to waste Defendants’ time and money,” their lawyers wrote.

The new dispute grew out of Howard’s bid to change his lawsuit again. He asked to swap one draft of his proposed sixth amended complaint for a new, 73-page version before the dismissal hearing.

His fifth amended complaint was still the version before the court.

Howard wanted Judge Hwang to read his new draft before deciding whether to let him change his claims and keep the case alive.

Diddy’s lawyers argued that Howard had not shown an emergency. They said he could seek changes through the usual process, which would give each side time to address them.

Howard, who represents himself, argued that his changes would narrow the dispute. He said the defense could address them at the hearing and offered to let its lawyers file a short response.

“The Application changes no deadline and adds no briefing. The revision narrows what Defendants must defend: one cause of action is withdrawn entirely, and another is limited to a single Defendant,” Howard wrote in his October 15 memorandum.

He said he reviewed the defense replies, Diddy’s criminal trial record and his own memory before seeking the changes. He argued that waiting for the usual process could leave the judge weighing claims he had since corrected.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Howard sought to remove claims that he was confined for about 12 hours during a December 2016 Miami encounter and that Diddy’s security team took his belongings. He said he concluded those statements were inaccurate. Those corrections came in his October 15 papers, before the new defense response.

Cassie also fought the proposed changes in a separate October 19 brief. Her lawyers said Howard raised new legal theories she had not had a fair chance to address. They also argued that he had not shown why the request was urgent.

Her team asked Judge Hwang to deny the request. Her lawyers attached an unsigned proposed order for the judge to consider. It was not a ruling.

The filings listed the dismissal hearing for October 21 before Judge Hwang.

item.title: Soulja Boy Warns France Unrest Should Put World Leaders On Notice
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Soulja Boy's France warning drew a class-politics joke as he urged governments to hear people squeezed by the cost of living.
item.content:encoded:
Soulja Boy called on world leaders to pay attention to France, warning that people struggling with the cost of living could only take so much before their anger boiled over.

The rapper weighed in on X on Sunday, saying rising prices had left everyday people working hard while barely getting by. “What’s happening in France is a wake-up call to the entire world,” he wrote.

His message prompted some wordplay in the replies. X user @emptystun wrote, “Crank that class consciousness,” turning the title of Soulja Boy’s breakout hit into a joke about his focus on working people.

The economic demands behind the French demonstrations were laid out by the CGT union ahead of Saturday’s mobilization. In its statement last week, the union backed calls for higher wages and pensions, lower prices and public services that met people’s needs. It said its members would join students, workers and retirees where conditions allowed. It also described access to health care as an essential right.

In a follow-up statement on Saturday, the CGT urged the government to negotiate with student and worker unions and address the demands through parliamentary debate. It also called for peaceful protests to continue, with higher pay, pensions and minimum social benefits among its demands.

The union estimated that nearly 800,000 young people, workers, unemployed people and retirees had joined gatherings across France that day. It framed the mobilization as part of a movement that had been building for several weeks.

Soulja Boy’s comments came just over a week after he floated a move into public service. AllHipHop covered his 2028 presidential tease earlier this month, when he said he was exploring how his work in music, business and technology could translate into that role.

FOX 5 Atlanta reported last week that he had identified economic opportunity, criminal justice reform, education and technology, including artificial intelligence, as areas of interest. At the time of that report, he had not announced a formal campaign, named a political party or released a detailed platform.

He closed Sunday’s post with an appeal to governments:

“Governments need to start listening to the people before frustration turns into chaos.”

item.title: Cardi B Found Missing Birkin Esmeralda After Studio Tip
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B shared the studio clue behind her missing Birkin Esmeralda, a day after she feared she had left the purse at a hotel.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B said last week that she found Esmeralda, the Hermès Birkin she feared she had left at a hotel. Her update pointed to a studio.

“UPDATE!! I found her!!!!” she wrote on X, quoting her earlier post about the lost bag.

A screenshot of a text exchange supplied the clue. “It’s in Kollin’s studio,” one message read. Cardi expressed relief in her reply. The other person said the bag should still be there and offered to bring it next time.

She had shared the loss with fans a day earlier. A fan had asked her to bring Esmeralda back out. In that post, the fan shared an old clip of the brown leather purse. Cardi responded that she had lost it and thought she might have left it behind at a hotel.

She described Esmeralda as the only bag she could not find and said she felt sad about the loss. AllHipHop’s earlier report covered that exchange. Her follow-up gave fans a far more hopeful account of where the bag had ended up.

Her love of rare bags had sent her on long hunts before. In a July 2023 Vogue feature, she joked that buying a bag had brought her to Paris while she attended the couture shows.

“I really came here to buy a Birkin bag,” she said. She added that she had spent two months hunting for one she could not find in the United States.

Her taste for those pieces also led to a business deal. Fashionphile named her its 2026 global brand ambassador on May 20. Its “Get Your Bag” campaign featured Cardi with pre-owned luxury accessories and paired shopping with resale.

She also chose a group of bags and other accessories from Hermès, Chanel and Goyard for the site. The company shot the campaign in New York City. It used both photos and video.

Sarah Davis, Fashionphile’s founder and president, said the rapper understood the value of those pieces. She said Cardi could help change how people thought about resale.

“I love a good bag, but I love a smart buy too,” Cardi said in the launch announcement.

item.title: Jadakiss’ Son Says He Hates Biggie’s “Ready To Die” Album Right In Front Of Biggie’s Son!
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Jadakiss' son Jae'Won shocks Biggie's son CJ Wallace by declaring his hatred for "Ready to Die," igniting a generational debate.
item.content:encoded:
What in the heck is going on?

Jadakiss‘ son Jae’Won might have committed a Hip-Hop felony by telling Biggie Smalls‘ son that he hates one of the most celebrated rap albums ever recorded. And he said it right to his face!

Now, I have heard some controversial opinions in my lifetime, but this one deserves a congressional hearing by the gods of Rap. Elders, where are y’all? Kiss, get ya boy!

During an episode of their “Silver Spoons” podcast, Jae’Won and Christopher “CJ” Wallace got into a spirited discussion about The Notorious B.I.G.’s legendary debut, Ready to Die. Jae’Won apparently had no reservations about criticizing the album that helped establish his podcast partner’s father as a rap icon.

“I hate the first album, not going to lie,” Jae’Won admitted.

Excuse me?

CJ was stunned.

“That’s wild,” CJ responded, before adding, “We might need a timeout on that one.”

Jae’Won wasn’t finished. He argued that Biggie’s second album, Life After Death, was a superior artistic achievement because it demonstrated greater maturity, stronger storytelling and more sophisticated production.

“The whole album (Ready To Die) is just very chaotic,” he said. “It’s not cohesive enough for me.”

Now, here’s where I have to intervene.

Ready to Die was released in 1994, when New York Hip-Hop was experiencing a renaissance. The album was grimy, cinematic, funny, disturbing and brutally personal. That chaos Jae’Won dislikes? Some might argue that was precisely the point.

Biggie was documenting the psychological turmoil of a young man navigating poverty, street life, ambition and impending superstardom!

And let’s remember something else. Without Ready to Die, there probably isn’t a Life After Death as we know it. Come on.

Jae’Won praised “Juicy,” “Big Poppa,” “One More Chance” and “Dreams,” suggesting those records would have been better suited for the second album.

He acknowledged Biggie’s excellence as an MC.

“The rapping on Ready to Die was dope as hell, but the songs overall were just like, I could have done without some of the songs,” he reasoned.

Listen, everybody is entitled to an opinion. Even when that opinion sounds like somebody walked into the Louvre and complained about the paintings. I think he’s too young and does not have any connection to the source material.

This is all generational! These are two sons of Hip-Hop royalty discussing the work of one of the genre’s greatest artists.

CJ defended his father’s debut, but Jae’Won stood his ground. MEH.

Let me try to be objective. Is Jae’Won hearing something the older generation refuses to acknowledge, or is he missing the historical point that made Ready to Die extraordinary? I think it is the latter.

What does Jadakiss think about all this?

Because I would pay good money to hear THAT conversation. What the…lol…or Tha Whut!

item.title: Kai Cenat Sets Japan Return With Ray For October 21
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kai Cenat's new trailer nods to the Tokyo meeting that brought Ray into his streams, ahead of their planned Japan return.
item.content:encoded:
Kai Cenat set an October 21 Japan stream with Ray, the friend he first met in the country in 2023. He rolled out the trip with a skit that nodded to their first chat on a Tokyo street.

The two-minute “Returning To Japan | Official Trailer” went up on Kai Cenat Live on Sunday. Its description sent fans to a scheduled stream called “RETURNING TO JAPAN W/ RAY.”

The skit played up car talk and a character dubbed “Bankroll Ray.” It also recalled their first chat at a Tokyo 7-Eleven. By the end, the script called for a flight back to Japan and “a little reset.”

In a GQ Taiwan interview last year, Ray looked back on that meeting in the summer of 2023.

Ray was on a school trip in Japan when he learned Cenat was streaming nearby. He followed clues from the broadcast to find him and asked for a photo. The encounter played out live for Cenat’s viewers. He told GQ he had only wanted a picture. He feared he might never get another chance to meet Cenat.

Ray told GQ he saw Cenat and the AMP crew as brothers. He said their bond off camera matched what fans saw on stream.

Cenat invited Ray to the United States to make content, then went to Taiwan himself. Local broadcaster FTV covered his visit with Ray in February 2024. They stopped in Taipei’s Ximending and Xinyi areas. Fans brought food and gifts as Cenat streamed his travels.

The pair also took their chemistry into a short film. They starred in the 2023 short “Global Pursuit,” an action comedy built around two cops and a sting. TV Guide’s cast listing credited Cenat as Miller and Ray as Shadow. The film drew on the “Rush Hour” setup made famous by Chris Tucker and Jackie Chan.

Ray later made room for Cenat in his GQ Sports “10 Essentials” appearance, released in March 2025.

“My next essential, Kai,” he said. He recalled meeting Cenat near a 7-Eleven in Japan. He summed up how far they had come: “here we are now.”

Their next shared stream is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21, on Kai Cenat Live.
